label: Late original-phase input of b/e/0/w/g/m/z/o after an x/1/r/s/n/f/h/c/l token
explanation: Fires almost only in the original (input) phase, essentially never at the delimiter or during copy. It never fires at t=0, rarely at t=1, and its rate climbs with position (about 25% of steps at orig_idx 6-8), with most mass on the last few inputs before <DEL>. It depends on the current input token: b, e, 0, w, g, m, z and o carry about 88% of the mass, while many other tokens almost never trigger it. It also depends on what came earlier: it is strongest when the prefix contains tokens such as x, 1, r, s, n, f, h, c, l (the top examples have prefixes like 1 f 1, 1 n x 1, s 1 r 1 1), and it rarely fires on a repeated token (in_first). Requiring at least two of those prefix tokens raises precision to about 0.80 but lowers recall. This looks like a graded mix of current-token and prefix content, likely a weighted sum, and the boolean predicate captures it only partly: false positives are mostly the right token after the wrong kind of prefix, and the 18% of mass it misses comes from other tokens such as q, a, u and 2.
